title: A Risk to Address: Which Trade-off?
context: A critical application server runs an unsupported version. A public exploit exists. You must conduct the risk analysis and propose a treatment.

n1.text: First step of the risk management process?

choices.text: Assess impact and likelihood before any decision
choices.why: Identifying then analyzing (impact × likelihood) precedes choosing the treatment.

choices.text: Accept the risk because no attack has been observed yet
choices.why: The absence of an incident is not an analysis; acceptance must be a documented last resort.
Remediation is likely justified, but without analysis you cannot prioritize or justify it.

n2.text: The incident would cost €40,000 and the annual likelihood is 3 occurrences. What is the ALE?

choices.why: €40,000 is the SLE (loss per occurrence), not the annual ALE.
That is division; ALE is the multiplication of loss by frequency.

n3.text: The patch costs €20,000 and reduces frequency to 1 occurrence/year. How do you classify the treatment?

choices.why: The control reduces frequency: it is mitigation. The net benefit is €60,000/year.
Transference delegates the loss; it does not reduce incident frequency.
Avoidance removes the activity causing the risk, which is not necessary here.

n4.outcome: You followed the process: analysis, SLE/ALE/ARO quantification, then treatment selection and benefit calculation.

debrief: Analysis: impact × likelihood, before choosing the treatment.
SLE = loss per incident; ALE = SLE × ARO (annual frequency).
Mitigation = reduce impact or likelihood; acceptance remains a documented, dated last resort.
